newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa extends fall on book-squaring.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa extends fall on book-squaring.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures fell further towards the close on Thursday on month-end book-squaring, but conditions were thin, traders said.
"It came down further on end-month MOC (market-on-close) selling as people squared their books," said one.
September failed at the key chart point of 1,028 stg a tonne, the most recent high, and retreated to a low of 1,013 stg. It stood eight down at 1,016.
"It now faces resistance up to 1,028," the trader said. After regaining a foothold above 1,000 recently, the market might not find enough follow-through buying to propel it much higher.
But traders said cocoa was still vulnerable to further upside moves given the positive technical outlook.
"It's more likely to go higher," said one. But any rise, as in previous sessions, was unlikely to be backed by heavy volume, they said.
Traders said they were still looking for a test through 1,030-1,035 on September following this week's high of 1,028.
Overall volume was a modest 2,535 lots.
The Dec/March spread widened to 21 stg from 14.
Traders said news the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) raised this season's deficit to 134,000 tonnes from its earlier estimate of 115,000 had no impact.
News of a routine ICCO buffer stock sale had probably been digested.
The ICCO said the higher cocoa deficit estimate reflected a 20,000-tonne cut in its crop forecast to 2.695 million tonnes. There was basically no change in the grindings estimate of 2.80 million.
In other news, cocoa bean exports from Nigeria fell to 861 tonnes in May from 5,994 tonnes a year earlier, official data from the Federal Produce Inspection Agency showed.
Cumulative exports for the first eight months of the 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) year totalled 126,324 tonnes, against 112,644 tonnes by the end of May 1996.
Total exports for the 1995/96 season reached 139,063 tonnes.
